verdict.rationale: Twenty's webhook docs state that it sends an HTTP POST to a user-supplied URL whenever a record is created, updated, or deleted. That is a first-party outbound event subscription a programmatic consumer can receive. The evidence is a single line, though, so the depth of the feature is unproven. Inbound webhook triggers (twenty-docs-63) and workflow HTTP-request steps are adjacent features and are not credited. Missing for 10: documented registration and management flow (UI/API) for webhook endpoints, event-type filtering, payload schema, signature verification, retry/delivery guarantees, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Twenty sends an HTTP POST to your URL whenever a record is created, updated, or deleted.
